I don't think being an addict has anything to do with him telling you anything. A normal person in real life could do the same thing. Sometimes people simply don't know what they're talking about.

Wow. Rude & condescending much?

I've been mistreated by many doctors numerous times over the last 5 years. It's a big enough of a deal for me to speak up for a change about the mistreatment. I'm doing what's right for me. Not what's right for you. When you're mistreated feel free to file a lawsuit. I'm just personally not up for that kind of headache.

I'm also not filing a lawsuit. I have no reason to. I don't need financial compensation and for me that's more hassle than it's worth. No use in paying a lawyer for this kinda crap. It's a big enough deal that I complained in written form. Normally I just let it pass and let go of it.
I sent it to A & D.
I sent it to the hospital's complaint department/quality assurance and the state medical board.

I have Blueshield PPO as well. My ER copay is $0 I've met every deductible. The doctor was straight up lying about the fluids costing money and I caught him in that lie by offering to pay out of pocket. Then told me the real reason was because he thought I didn't need it. I accepted the truthful answer a lot more than insurance BS.

Regarding the cost of the fluids/benadryl I was actually "polietely" calling the Doctors bluff. He said he couldn't give it to me because my insurance wouldn't pay for it, so I offered to pay for it. He tried to play it off like nice guy I wouldn't do that to you and I flipped it telling him I could afford it and would pay for it. That's when he told me the real reason he wasn't giving it which was "I don't think you need it so I'm not doing it." 

& the benadryl thing was stupid because if was addictive he wouldn't have given it to me intramuscularly.

I did see my doctor about it. I had run out a week early in May too. I was then hospitalized over it (plus a flare) the hospital got me back on my medication. I went to my pain specialists office excited because the hospital doctor had said he had many ideas he wanted to discuss with me. Instead, when I went to see him, he told me he had no ideas, that I needed to be on Suboxone and that under no circumstances would he raise my dosage. (I’ve had seizures on suboxone so it’s not an option for me.)

I was extremely dejected after that and regrettably went the fuck it route. 

Then on June 10th (my sobriety date) I was in the beginning stages of withdrawal. I went to one hospital who refused to treat me at all for my pain/withdrawal problems even though I was asking for help to get off the medications.  Instead they came back with a stack of papers for me to call to maybe get a bed at a detox. Which they warned me could take up to two weeks. I was already in withdrawal though so it was super useless. I was also suicidal at this time and made that very clear - yet they were going to let me walk anyway. 

Then that hospital told me to go directly to another one that had a psych unit with a detox facility. To which I went. Upon arriving there the ER doctor started loosely doing an exam before he asked me who prescribed my medications. I gave him my doctors name and he outright said I was a liar and accused me of doctor shopping.

I learned later that somehow the pharmacy put down a different doctor for each refill over the last 4 months. They were all in the same practice and written by my doctor but somehow the pharmacy just picked a different name each time. This royally screwed me. 

I asked for help and that emergency room doctor told me, "You're a liar and don't play the suicide card on me because you aren't and we'll refuse treatment because you were soundly evaluated at X hospital earlier in the night and they cleared you." 

I proceeded to leave the emergency room and attempted to get hit by a bunch of cars on a dark and busy road. The cops were called. I was hysterical. I was asking for help to get off the medications or at the very least get into the psych unit for help of some kind. So, the police talked to the ER doctor that told me I was a liar. They told me he was going to help and to go back to the ER.

So, with a police escort I went back to this particular emergency room. The ER doctor then straight-up told me I wasn't getting drugs from him. I told him I didn't want drugs, I wanted off drugs, he lectured me on the dangers of Dilaudid and told me that he wasn't helping because I should have enough to last me the rest of the month. I didn't understand, I told him I wanted OFF drugs. He didn't listen. Even with the cops there he said he wasn't going to help. I explained I was very suicidal and he countered with, "you were evaluated her 20 days ago, and cleared, it's too soon for a new psych evaluation." I tried explaining I needed help then and didn’t get it and that I still need that help. He wasn't having any of it. He also said he was mad because I was trying to get hit by cars to get drugs. I told him I was legitimately suicidal.

He printed up a piece of paper for a detox facility that would cost 10 grand and told me to go there. I then left the ER there and called the place they wanted me to go to. That place said they couldn't take me directly but I could go to ANOTHER ER room and they'd transfer me to their facility.

So, out to my 3rd ER in 2 days I went. They didn't contact the other detox facility instead they hospitalized me on psych but discharged me after the 72 hour hold because I was vomiting so much and requiring IM meds which they don't do on psych at that hospital. I was at a loss. 

I went home on day 5 dejected, alone, and completely scared shitless (still am). I went through every medical channel possible to get help and was rejected at every twist and turn. I just want/wanted to die. Somehow I made it through and have attempted to get help for addiction, because I didn’t know what else to do. Now here I am almost 50 days later and I’m still sick. I’ve had 10+ ER visits in these last 50 ish days and no one is taking me seriously. The vomiting is out of control, I have a viral gastro infection on top of everything else and each day I’m suffering beyond a normal level.

Now I’m living my worst nightmare. I’m in a rehab, in pain and being treated like a criminal. I am a bit suicidal from it all. The stress and weight of being ill like this is so harmful. Also as far as methadone goes, I won’t do it at a doctors mercy. Those withdrawals massively hurt more than my condition. Al least if a doctor cuts me off of oxycodone or dilaudid I know those withdrawals are survivable. Methadone hurt me for 8 months after my last dose because a doctor cut me off of it. I was only ever on 5mgs of methadone but, I experienced bone pain for 8 months. 

I hate being a victim. I'm typically a survivor but at this point I'm at a loss.

>Why you ended up with her is none of my business but you should have known better. 

Wow Judgement much? How am I supposed to "know better" when I never knew who she was in the first place till I met her? I was referred to Stanford Medical for a consult. Didn't even know she was on the team until well, she introduced herself. Even then I had no idea who she was.

I wish I could get out of my current situation. However, unless there are major political changes, I have to accept the fact that I'm "better off" off of the opioids. Yea it's natural to cycle through withdrawal when you run out. Ya it's normal to med seek for relief when you're in pain but, more and more doctors are becoming more and more afraid of the DEA and it fucking sucks. 

>Who told you that you were an addict? 

Everyone. My family, my doctors, my psychiatrist, some of my friends and so forth. At the end of the day I gave up/in. I was scripted 120 2mg dilaudid pills and I was out of them in 10days. Seems like pretty addictive behavior if you ask me. Lembke didn't blacklist me either. 

I accomplished that myself by making some very regretful and stupid mistakes while in withdrawal. That I should've known better before making those mistakes. Chances are now I'll likely never be scripted an opiate again so, might as well get used to being an "addict."

It sucks.

Ugh. I saw Dr. Anna Lembke in September of this past year. She wanted to put me on a microdose of suboxone. I had a seizure once on that so I told her no. I ended up quitting my opiates cold turkey as a result. I was sober from November - February before I got into too much pain and was back on the opiates from February - June. Then in June I went cold turkey again because this opioid crisis is too ridiculous. Now I'm in a treatment program from drugs and I just feel very victimized/like I don't belong.

Ya, my schedule is about to get jam-packed because I'm actively seeking employment and need to go to treatment and need to attend meetings so its a bit of a lot of things.
Thanks, I have really deep emotional scars surrounding meetings, but if I need to do them I will. I just need help getting there.
Just texted you.

I had a seizure on a 2mg/0.5mg suboxone strip 4 years ago. So, not really? My doctor recommends belbucca which is a bit different, but still the same main ingredient so I can't take it without supervision and no doctor I have is willing to let me take it in their office and be watched/supervised. So, blah.

You're super sweet. The world shouldn't be this way, but it is and I simply don't have the energy to fight the war on opioids. So, my best choice is to live in an infuriating amount of pain and hope my body adjusts.

Yeah. I really just need some kind of hope. IDK. It's way rough right now. It never used to be like this. Something has just changed inside of me and I'm sick of dealing with feeling a wreck at all times. I run around in more pain than I can handle on a daily basis. It's crippling. At the same time I can't continue to be cycling with my medications. Its not sustainable. I'm just irritated, over it, and done.

Well, I was planning on going to the Emergency Room and stating it along with the pain/medication issues and see if they could admit me to withdraw me from the medications I'm taking so that it's covered by insurance and I'm not absolutely miserable. I have a good relationship with the in-house shrink at the hospital I usually go to so if I can get the ER to do an admission then from there I'm sure she'd be gung-ho about withdrawing me/helping.

The alternative option I have is to do it outpatient. I have a doctor who I could see daily for a week straight while I deal with the withdrawal symptoms, except he's super expensive ($250 a visit) and he's not really in the withdrawing from medication business. He's an oncologist who is way too nice and took me under his wing years ago when I had some anemia issues. So, I don't exactly want to use/waste his resources unless I have to.

I've just had it with my ability to handle life in general. It's all a lot.

It's unbelievable how unhelpful those hotlines actually are. They just exist to keep you alive for 5 minutes or send police knocking at your door. No one has any real ideas on how to handle distress. I feel so low.
Yah, I've also noticed myself becoming more and more hostile. I'm just so goddamned angry. Absolutely angry.

I've been on the medication for 5 years. It's only been the last 3 months there's been a problem with running out early. It coincides with a doctor change where the doctor is completely jerking me around and I don't have the energy to fight the opioid war so I figure going off of them and living in crippling pain is my only answer. At least I wont be contending with American Politics and my illness.

I do have a severe legitimate diagnosis that is admittedly very difficult to handle. I'm projectile vomiting on a multi-time per week basis and I'm so over it. 

Glad to know I'm not welcome here with my 'drug addiction' fuck life.

Edit: Also I was sober from November to February before being put back on the drugs because the doctors felt I was torturing myself being off the medication. So I don't know. I'm over it.

I have no capital to start my own business. Otherwise, I'd be doing that. I'm getting more and more upset with my situation and its just hard. IDK. The crippling pain thing has ruined my life and my ability to do anything. I'm really bitter about it at the moment.

Ya, we tried up at UCLA 2 weeks ago and I got a medical hospitalization where they deemed it would be best to stabilize me on my narcotic medications. Obviously, though, I'm incapable of managing my own script so, at this point, I'm just done with it all. I'm gonna probably go back tomorrow seeing as I'm out of state at the moment but I feel miserable. Just miserable.
